title: Autorelay Runbook Orchestrator: idempotent incident playlet runner
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an 'Autorelay Runbook Orchestrator' service that executes vetted runbook playlets as idempotent, permissioned tasks. The service should accept a compact runbook DSL, schedule and run discrete steps (checks, remediation, notifications), enforce RBAC and dry-run capabilities, and emit structured telemetry. This ticket covers the core runtime, safety gates (approval/timeout), and an initial set of playlets for common support flows (node-restart, autoscale-rollback, prefix-cache-warm).
acceptance_criteria: Runtime accepts JSON/YAML playlet and validates against schema
Each step executes with at-least-once semantics but runlets are idempotent by default
RBAC enforced via service-to-service token mapping and audit logs sent to central audit stream
Dry-run mode produces a full plan and predicted side-effects without making mutations
Telemetry emitted per-step: duration_ms, outcome, user/actor, inputs-hash
Canary rollout: 5% of operator-triggered runbooks upstreamed to oncall namespace
Integration test demonstrating automated remediation for a simulated KV cache overflow
technical_design: Core components: (1) Playlet parser + validator (schema v1), (2) Executor with step sandboxing and retry/backoff policies, (3) Permission layer mapping Linear/Galaxy operator roles to allowed runlet families, (4) Audit/telemetry writer (EventBridge -> BigQuery), (5) Dry-run planner and human-approval webhook. Implementation will be a small Go service using existing helix-cluster agent lib for privileged actions and the opsctl credential broker for token exchange. Steps will run in isolated containers (gVisor-lite) to reduce blast radius and support resource limits.
safety_tradeoffs: We prefer strong safety checks over speed for initial rollout. Default mode will be 'manual-approval' for any runlet that mutates customer-visible resources; automated remediation will be opt-in per-runlet. Idempotency is enforced by step-level dedupe keys stored in the runbook state store (Dynamo/Redis). To reduce risk, the first set of runlets will not include destructive DB migrations or schema changes. Timeouts are conservative (step default 3m) and an emergency abort path is provided via oncall console.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): local runner + unit tests (2 weeks). Phase 1 (internal alpha): internal ops team only, dry-run + manual approval (1 week). Phase 2 (canary): 5% of incidents run with auto-execute for non-customer-impacting runlets (2 weeks). Phase 3 (general availability): open to platform SREs with full telemetry and policy guardrails (3 weeks). Post-GA: expand runlet library and add UI wiring in console.
integration_points: opsctl credential broker (ENG-7934) for token exchange
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: rogue runlet accidents -> Mitigation: require signature/approval on all mutating steps during alpha
Risk: non-idempotent scripts -> Mitigation: mandate idempotency test harness and enforce input hashing
Risk: telemetry gaps -> Mitigation: block GA until step-level metrics are covered by SLO alerts
qa_notes: Provide deterministic simulation harness that seeds a fake cluster and asserts pre/post invariants. Tests should include cancellation mid-step, retry paths, and recovery after executor restart. Add property tests for idempotency and schema fuzzing for playlet parser.
